accepted.sentence: People often arrange volumes with their spines facing outward, making titles easier to scan and retrieve.
To remove an item from a tightly packed row, neighboring volumes may be shifted aside before it is drawn out.
After use, items are returned to an open space, often grouped by subject, author, or size.
Decorative objects and framed photographs may share the storage space with reading materials.
Periodic dusting clears exposed surfaces and item tops, especially when stored contents remain uncovered.
Volumes are usually stood upright; unusually tall ones may be laid flat to avoid overhanging.
Weighted end supports can keep upright volumes from leaning into gaps at the ends of a row.
During rearrangement, items may be temporarily removed so the storage positions can be changed or cleaned.
